learningObjectives: Explain what an Approval Step does and when to use it
Describe how Approve and Reject outcomes route the Case to different paths
Configure a single approval with routing and outcome paths

elements.description: A user decision controls the approval path. Choose the reviewer and configure both outcomes.

elements.text: Think of a budget checkpoint: choose the person allowed to decide, then write down what an acceptance and a rejection mean. The checkpoint alone does not promise email, escalation or automatic approval.

elements.description: Default rejection resolves the request as Resolved-Rejected. Revision requires an explicit destination; it is not implied by the word Reject.
Approval can continue work or select a Stage, with an optional status update. Rejection can resolve, continue, or select a Stage.
Enabled email or mobile approval lets the routed stakeholder decide outside the application. Check the recipient and enablement rather than assuming every Step sends these notifications.

elements.caption: A simplified decision model; rework is an explicit configuration choice.

elements.description: A single approval may use a named recipient, request-dependent routing, or a shared queue. Several required decisions need an explicit sequence or a cascade.
Choose between one particular reviewer and any eligible reviewer. Do not turn a shared Assignment into a claim that all queue members receive independent approvals.
Reporting structure follows manager relationships. Authority matrix supplies an ordered list and can include other departments. The next module explores both.

elements.caption: Different policies require different numbers and destinations of decisions.

examPitfalls.title: Universal Send back
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The standard decision pair is Approve/Reject; a revision destination must be designed.

examPitfalls.title: Default rejection
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Rejection does not inherently return work to the previous user.

examPitfalls.title: One versus many
examPitfalls.trapDescription: One shared queue Assignment is not a parallel cascade.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Count required decisions before choosing a model.

examPitfalls.title: Status inference
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A label alone does not prove where the next Assignment is.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect configured flow and execution evidence.

examPitfalls.title: Notifications
examPitfalls.trapDescription: External approval requires the corresponding option to be enabled.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Any authorized regional manager may decide a loan request. Only one decision is required. Which design fits?

options.text: One Approve/Reject Step routed to the managers’ shared Work Queue
A cascade that broadcasts three independent decisions simultaneously
Automatically assign the decision to the applicant
Replace the human decision with automatic approval

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish one shared Assignment from several required approvals.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A shared queue lets an eligible manager handle the single decision. A cascade is an ordered series, not an any-one broadcast.

optionExplanations.A: A shared queue lets an eligible manager handle the single decision.
optionExplanations.B: A cascade is an ordered series, not an any-one broadcast.
optionExplanations.C: The applicant is not an authorized manager in this requirement.
optionExplanations.D: Automatic approval removes the required human review.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A purchase requires the department head’s approval before the CFO may review it. Which sequence satisfies this policy?

options.text: Department-head Approval Step followed by CFO Approval Step on the approved path
Send both decisions simultaneously and count the first reply
Let the requester approve instead of the department head
Skip the department-head Assignment using an automatic flag

practiceQuiz.hint: The CFO must wait for the first approval.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Two ordered gates preserve the required dependency. Simultaneous review does not preserve department-head-first ordering.

optionExplanations.A: Two ordered gates preserve the required dependency.
optionExplanations.B: Simultaneous review does not preserve department-head-first ordering.
optionExplanations.C: The requester cannot substitute for the specified department head.
optionExplanations.D: A flag without the required human decision does not satisfy the policy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: One manager must approve an expense claim before reimbursement. No separate review confirmation is required. What is the simplest design?

options.text: One Approval Step with configured routing and outcomes
Two mandatory Approval Steps because every approval requires confirmation
A cascade is mandatory whenever the recipient is a manager
An optional action that lets reimbursement continue before sign-off

practiceQuiz.rationale: One gate provides the one required manager decision. A second mandatory decision duplicates a requirement that does not exist.

optionExplanations.A: One gate provides the one required manager decision.
optionExplanations.B: A second mandatory decision duplicates a requirement that does not exist.
optionExplanations.C: A manager recipient does not itself require a multi-level chain.
optionExplanations.D: Optional work cannot guarantee this mandatory gate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Each request must be approved by its own designated manager. Which design adapts the recipient to the request?

options.text: Use configured routing logic to identify that request’s manager
Assign every request to the same CFO
Use any-manager shared routing despite the specific-manager requirement
Route by a fixed alphabetical list unrelated to the request

practiceQuiz.hint: The destination must follow the request’s business relationship.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Request-dependent routing selects the relevant manager. A fixed CFO ignores different designated managers.

optionExplanations.A: Request-dependent routing selects the relevant manager.
optionExplanations.B: A fixed CFO ignores different designated managers.
optionExplanations.C: Any eligible queue member is insufficient when one particular manager is required.
optionExplanations.D: Alphabetical ordering does not encode the required business relationship.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Rejected requests must return to the Revision Stage for corrections. Where should this behavior be configured?

options.text: Configure the Reject flow to change to the Revision Stage
Assume every approval includes a standard Send back outcome
Leave default rejection unchanged and expect revision
Change the button label without changing flow

practiceQuiz.hint: Presentation alone does not set the rejection destination.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An explicit rejection destination implements the revision policy. Approve/Reject does not establish a universal third Send back outcome.

optionExplanations.A: An explicit rejection destination implements the revision policy.
optionExplanations.B: Approve/Reject does not establish a universal third Send back outcome.
optionExplanations.C: Default rejection resolves as Resolved-Rejected, rather than this revision route.
optionExplanations.D: A label change does not configure the destination.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A manager must approve a request from an email without opening the application. Which approval feature addresses this?

options.text: Enable email approval for the configured approval recipient
Assume every approval sends an actionable email automatically
Replace routing with an unrelated email address in a label
Wait for a timeout to count as the manager’s approval

practiceQuiz.hint: Enable the channel that carries the decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Email approval allows the routed recipient to decide outside the application. The approval option must be enabled; it is not an unconditional notification guarantee.

optionExplanations.A: Email approval allows the routed recipient to decide outside the application.
optionExplanations.B: The approval option must be enabled; it is not an unconditional notification guarantee.
optionExplanations.C: A display label does not determine who receives the approval.
optionExplanations.D: Elapsed time does not establish the requested human decision.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which pair of outcomes defines the Approve/Reject Step?

options.text: Approve and Reject
Submit and Cancel only
Withdraw and Escalate only
Forward and Archive only

practiceQuiz.rationale: Approve and Reject are the two decision outcomes covered here. Submit and Cancel do not describe this decision pair.

optionExplanations.A: Approve and Reject are the two decision outcomes covered here.
optionExplanations.B: Submit and Cancel do not describe this decision pair.
optionExplanations.C: Withdrawal and escalation are not substitutes for the approval decision.
optionExplanations.D: Forwarding and archiving do not express approval or rejection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A manager rejects a request and no custom rejection flow has been configured. Which default status does the source describe?

options.text: Resolved-Rejected
Deleted without a Case record
Pending-Approval until the requester cancels
Automatically escalated to the CEO

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish default rejection from explicitly configured rework.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Default rejection changes status to Resolved-Rejected. Resolution is not deletion.

optionExplanations.A: Default rejection changes status to Resolved-Rejected.
optionExplanations.C: Leaving an approval pending is not the stated default rejected outcome.
optionExplanations.D: Executive escalation requires its own design; it is not the default.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Case must display Approved when the approval succeeds. Which configuration directly addresses this?

options.text: Configure the optional Case status change for the approved outcome
Require a second HR approval just to change status
Create a separate Case Type solely to display the status
Assume clicking Approve always sets the exact label Approved

practiceQuiz.rationale: The approved outcome supports an optional status update. An extra approval adds work without supplying this configuration.

optionExplanations.A: The approved outcome supports an optional status update.
optionExplanations.B: An extra approval adds work without supplying this configuration.
optionExplanations.C: A separate Case Type is unnecessary for this status requirement.
optionExplanations.D: A successful decision does not guarantee an arbitrary status label.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After approval, a request must proceed to a legal review Assignment. What connects the approved outcome to the remaining work?

options.text: Configure the approved flow to continue to the legal review
Put Legal in an invented second-approver field on a single approval
Treat the SLA deadline as the successful approval transition
Rely on a View label to launch the legal Assignment

practiceQuiz.rationale: The successful approval path can continue to the configured next work. A single approval does not supply an invented universal second-approver field.

optionExplanations.A: The successful approval path can continue to the configured next work.
optionExplanations.B: A single approval does not supply an invented universal second-approver field.
optionExplanations.C: A deadline is not the approved outcome.
optionExplanations.D: View text is not a workflow connection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A successful approval still displays Pending-Approval. The process has not been inspected. What is the justified next check?

options.text: Inspect configured outcome flow and Case status updates
Conclude the CFO Assignment must be waiting in a queue
Conclude an Access Role silently discarded the decision
Conclude the Case must wait for its SLA deadline

practiceQuiz.hint: A status label alone does not diagnose runtime routing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configuration and execution evidence are needed to explain the displayed status. The label does not prove a CFO Assignment exists or identify its destination.

optionExplanations.A: Configuration and execution evidence are needed to explain the displayed status.
optionExplanations.B: The label does not prove a CFO Assignment exists or identify its destination.
optionExplanations.C: There is no evidence here of an authorization failure.
optionExplanations.D: Nothing here establishes a deadline-based dependency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Process requires a user to decide whether to approve or reject work. Which Step represents that gate?

options.text: Approve/Reject
An automatic Decision with no user Assignment
A background Utility with no user Assignment
A status display View only

practiceQuiz.rationale: Approve/Reject represents the user’s approval decision. An automatic condition evaluation is not the required user review.

optionExplanations.A: Approve/Reject represents the user’s approval decision.
optionExplanations.B: An automatic condition evaluation is not the required user review.
optionExplanations.C: Background processing does not collect this decision.
optionExplanations.D: Displaying a status alone does not create an approval gate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO outcome configurations are supported for an Approval Step?

options.text: Approve can continue or change to a specified Stage
Reject can resolve, continue, or change to a specified Stage
Approve must always terminate the entire Case
Reject must delete the Case

practiceQuiz.rationale: Approval can follow continuation or a Stage destination. Rejection supports resolution, continuation or a Stage destination.

optionExplanations.A: Approval can follow continuation or a Stage destination.
optionExplanations.B: Rejection supports resolution, continuation or a Stage destination.
optionExplanations.C: Termination is not mandatory for every approval.
optionExplanations.D: Deletion is not the rejection flow contract.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Three managers must each approve a contract in order before it proceeds. Which TWO designs can represent the required series?

options.text: A cascade with an ordered authority-matrix approver list
Three sequential Approval Steps, one per manager
One shared Assignment where any single manager decides
Select just one manager randomly

practiceQuiz.hint: All three decisions are required, in order.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An ordered cascade can represent all three required parties. Three explicit gates can encode the same fixed sequence.

optionExplanations.A: An ordered cascade can represent all three required parties.
optionExplanations.B: Three explicit gates can encode the same fixed sequence.
optionExplanations.C: A single shared decision does not collect three approvals.
optionExplanations.D: Choosing only one manager omits two required decisions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO settings are part of configuring an Approval Step?

options.text: Choose a recipient such as a specific user or shared Work Queue
Define how approved and rejected outcomes proceed
Assume every approval automatically creates a child Case
Configure only Approve because Reject has no flow

practiceQuiz.rationale: Routing identifies who may handle the approval. Outcome flow determines what happens after the decision.

optionExplanations.A: Routing identifies who may handle the approval.
optionExplanations.B: Outcome flow determines what happens after the decision.
optionExplanations.C: Child Case creation is not inherent in this Step.
optionExplanations.D: Reject is a configurable outcome, not an absent path.

quickRecap.value: A user approves or rejects before the configured approval path proceeds.
One particular reviewer or any eligible reviewer in a shared queue.
Resolved-Rejected; configure a different flow for revision.
Use explicit ordered gates or a cascade, rather than treating shared work as several decisions.
